correctness.rationale: Prime-exponent vectors turn multiplicative dependence into rational linear dependence. Primitive Pluecker coordinates give a complete exact invariant of a two-plane for independent pairs, so monochromatic triangles are exactly unordered maximal-rank dependent triples. Exact enumeration through \(1215\) yields \(15\) consecutive triples, \(13\) through \(1000\) and precisely two new at \(1215\). Direct identities verify the boundary witnesses, and six permutations per unordered maximal-rank triple give \(M(1214)=78\) and \(M(1215)=90\). The finite scope is explicit; no inference about larger \(H\) is made.

value.rationale: The cutoff is mathematically motivated rather than arbitrary: \(H=1000\) is the only explicit census boundary quoted in the new primary paper, which also says the growth of \(M(H)\) is unknown. Determining the very next jump identifies the first new data point beyond that boundary, gives an exact natural invariant value, and links it to the exceptional Benelux pair. The exhaustive no-new-triple interval \(1001\)--\(1214\) is essential to the result, not a cosmetic computation.
